title: Asteria Retail — Integration playbook / POC sprint kickoff
summary: Kickoff for a 6-week POC to validate Redwood integration for Asteria's retail recommendation and chat assistant workloads. Main goals: verify OpenAI-compatible API parity, validate function/tool calling for inventory actions, measure latency/throughput with 2k-5k daily sessions, and produce structured JSON outputs for downstream analytics. Discussed dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, VPC/KMS constraints, benchmark plan and timeline. Agreed next steps: share benchmark template, set up sandbox keys, schedule infra run and bench week.
topics: workload sizing and synthetic load patterns
function/tool calling and structured output schema
transcript: 00:00 Maya Chen: thanks everyone for joining, we wanna run through the scope for the POC and make sure the success criteria are clear
00:08 Priya Raman: great thanks, were excited — main ask is we need parity with our current OpenAI endpoints for chat and functions and lower latency than what were seeing now
00:18 Jorge Alvarez: quick clarifying question, when you say parity, is it API shape only or model output quality as well?

00:23 Priya Raman: both — our front-end uses function calling heavily for inventory adjust and price checks. If function calling semantics or the JSON schema differs well break a bunch of infra, so compatibility is key
00:34 Evan Cole: we also have a batch async job that runs nightly to re-embed product catalog — embeddings throughput and cost matter for that path

00:41 Lina Park: noted, embeddings and streaming/chat are separate workload profiles. For the realtime chat were targeting p95 latency under 220ms for short contexts, and throughput ~40-60 reqs/s steady state

00:56 Sanjay Patel: security side: must use our KMS, require audit logs forwarded to Splunk and SAML SSO. On-prem option is a blocker for PCI-scoped processing, so we need to understand Private deployment timelines

01:10 Maya Chen: well cover private deployment cadence, but initial POC can run on Redwood Hosted with VPC peering and customer KMS integration — we usually do a sandbox key and a short validation sprint
01:22 Marni Lewis: timeline expectation — can we do benching and a functional pilot in 6 weeks?

01:27 Jorge Alvarez: yes, typical pattern is 2 weeks integration + SDK work, 1 week instrumented bench run, 2 weeks analysis and fixes, final week for handoff and decision. Well keep milestones weekly

01:40 Priya Raman: for workload sizing, heres rough traffic: peak storefront chat 200 concurrent sessions, average message size ~120 tokens, session length 6 messages. Nightly embeddings job is ~12 million tokens per month
01:56 Lina Park: that helps. For bench we'll simulate both bursty storefront traffic and steady background embedding jobs — can you send sample traffic traces?
02:04 Evan Cole: I can export traces, yes, will share post call

02:09 Jorge Alvarez: benchmark plan: we recommend a 3-part bench: 1) API parity smoke tests over OpenAI-compatible endpoints, 2) latency/throughput sweeps with varying batch sizes and KV cache warm/cold scenarios, 3) function calling fidelity checks with our sample function schemas and structured output validation
02:27 Priya Raman: how do you handle structured outputs? We rely on JSON schema enforcement and hallucination detection — sometimes models return arrays or miss required keys

02:35 Lina Park: we use prompt engineering + Redwood's structured-output mode that layers a lightweight validator and retries on schema failures. For high-volume paths we can run a post-processor validator in-stream to reject and re-ask, that shows up in the bench metrics as a schema-failure rate
02:47 Sanjay Patel: and how are retries counted for cost and latency? We need accurate accounting so cost models are realistic
02:53 Maya Chen: good point — bench will report tokens, retries, and end-to-end tail latencies; well tag synthetic workload so you can map to your cost model

03:01 Marni Lewis: on SDKs — we have a node/python stack and some services call the LLM directly via REST. We prefer an OpenAI-compatible endpoint so changes are minimal. Is Redwoods OpenAI-compat drop-in complete for function calls?

03:12 Jorge Alvarez: yes, we surface OpenAI-compatible endpoints for the common flows. There are small differences around streaming chunk formats and function calling edge cases — we document them. Part of the POC is a compatibility matrix test suite
03:26 Evan Cole: any gotchas with streaming or partial responses for small tokens? We have UI logic that expects interim deltas
03:32 Lina Park: streaming uses the same chunking idea but event framing may differ slightly; we can toggle a compatibility mode that emulates the expected chunk boundaries for your UI during the POC
03:42 Priya Raman: great. For benchmarks, we also want to validate quality: reranking accuracy and retrieval augmented responses — can Redwood run evals against our golden set?

03:50 Jorge Alvarez: yes please send a golden set of prompts and expected outputs. We will run generation metrics (ROUGE/BLEU not perfect, but we also do semantic similarity and human spot checks). We recommend ~1k-2k golden prompts for meaningful signal
04:03 Sanjay Patel: security again: for Hosted we need assurances on data retention and ability to disable logs for PII. Can you provide SOC2 and encryption details?
04:11 Maya Chen: we'll share the security pack — SOC 2 report, KMS integration guide, retention controls, and the audit log schema. Also we can mask or redact fields in transit if needed

04:21 Marni Lewis: acceptance criteria — to make the pilot a success we need: 1) <2% schema failure on structured outputs, 2) p95 latency <220ms for chat happy path, 3) embedding cost within 15% of our current baseline, 4) function calling fidelity >98% on smoke tests
04:39 Jorge Alvarez: agreed, we'll instrument everything and put dashboards in the Console so you can monitor tokens, failed schemas, retries, latency percentiles, and cost estimates
04:47 Priya Raman: for the nightly embed job we care about quantization and throughput — will Redwood provide quantized model variants?

04:54 Lina Park: yes, for private/dedicated we have quantized variants and kernel optimizations. For hosted POC we'll propose a cost/perf configuration and test against your embedding throughput requirement
05:04 Evan Cole: one more ops question — can we pin model versions and pin configs per route? we need stable regressions
05:10 Jorge Alvarez: yep route-level pinning and rollout policies (canary/A-B/fallback) are supported. We'll show you the rollout UI in the demo
05:18 Marni Lewis: any constraints on our infra for VPC peering?
05:22 Maya Chen: typical peer with a private subnet and a NAT; we'll share a checklist. For KMS youll supply a key ARN and well wire it up for encryption at rest
05:31 Priya Raman: what does the bench week look like exactly?

05:34 Jorge Alvarez: Week 3 we run a 5-day instrumented bench. Day 1 smoke/integration. Day 2 steady-state throughput. Day 3 peak burst and cold-cache tests. Day 4 function-calling fidelity and schema checks. Day 5 wrap and correlation to cost models
05:46 Marni Lewis: sample artifacts to share?
05:48 Evan Cole: I will share trace exports, sample JSON function specs, and our golden evaluation set

05:53 Maya Chen: well share: 1) bench template spreadsheet, 2) SDK quickstart repo with example function calls, 3) security pack. Links: https://redwood.link/pilot-bench-template , https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-quickstart (private), security doc: https://redwood.link/security-pack
06:06 Sanjay Patel: any initial blockers for compliance? We may require on-prem later but initial POC on Hosted with KMS is fine
06:12 Jorge Alvarez: no blockers — we'll scope the Private deployment path as a parallel track if pilot meets gating criteria
06:18 Marni Lewis: costs — can you give a rough estimate for the bench week so we can pre-approve spend?

06:23 Maya Chen: estimate depends on burst profile, but for your stated volumes and a 5-day stress run wed ballpark $3k-$7k for hosted bench compute, well provide an itemized estimate after we see the traces
06:33 Priya Raman: sounds reasonable, send the estimate and we'll route it through finance

06:36 Jorge Alvarez: integration notes — for minimal code change we recommend using Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoint plus the SDK in node for retries and structured output helpers. If you prefer pure REST we provide a compatibility shim
06:48 Evan Cole: ok question about observability: will traces and per-token breakdowns be available? we need to map cost to services
06:55 Lina Park: Console exposes per-route token buckets, cost breakdown, and trace links; we can also stream events to your observability via webhook
07:03 Marni Lewis: wrap-up and risks — biggest risk is function-calling nuances breaking UI logic, second is schema failure rate. We'll mitigate with the compatibility mode and validator
07:14 Maya Chen: good recap. who owns the shared artifacts?
07:18 Evan Cole: I will own exporting traces and schemas by Friday (2026-05-15),
07:23 Priya Raman: I'll review golden set and get it to you by next Tue (2026-05-19),
07:28 Maya Chen: Redwood will send bench template, SDK quickstart and security pack by EOD tomorrow (2026-05-12). We'll also schedule the bench week kickoff for Mon 2026-05-25
07:37 Sanjay Patel: one last detail — please include data retention controls in the security doc table for each env
07:42 Jorge Alvarez: will do; add it to the action items
07:45 Maya Chen: thanks all, well follow up with the shared links and calendar invites. Talk soon
